name: GettingStarted
title: Getting Started with HEPCAT
summary: Load the package, read a model and make a first spinor calculation.

sections.title: Load HEPCAT
paragraphs: These first examples introduce the expression format before constructing a small QED amplitude. They assume your checkout is in ~/code/hepcat. Change that path if you installed it elsewhere.

Load the package in a separate input cell. One [Get](paclet:ref/Get) command is enough; the loader finds its companion source files and registers the Help pages automatically. You do not need to set a global path variable.

examples.description: Load the package from its checkout. Change the path if your HEPCAT folder is elsewhere.

sections.title: Read a Model
paragraphs: A calculation begins with a model value returned by [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel). The bundled model numbered 2 supplies the QED interactions used in this example. Keep the returned value in a notebook variable and pass it to the functions that need the theory.

A constructive model has four parts: particle data, known interactions or amplitudes, independent parameters and dependent functions. `Length /@ qedModel` is a quick way to see the size of those parts, not the amplitude itself. [ModelParameterRules](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ModelParameterRules) shows the numerical assignments used by numerical checks.

examples.description: Locate the model directory and read the elementary QED model.
Obtain numerical mass and coupling rules from this model.

sections.title: Write and Reduce a Spinor Chain
paragraphs: [SpinorChain](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorChain) stores a bracket or a longer chain as ordinary Mathematica data. The following first expression displays an angle bracket. The second applies [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) to an angle bracket with the same massless spinor at both ends, which vanishes.
The label 1 identifies the first external particle; it is not a numerical momentum value. Expressions remain symbolic until you ask for a numerical evaluation or a validation check.

examples.description: Display <13> in the notebook.
Reduce a vanishing self-bracket.

sections.title: Construct a Complete Amplitude
paragraphs: Now give [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) the ordered external particle list and the two model roles. Here the process is four point, so products of three-point amplitudes suffice for factorization and the same QED model can serve both roles.

The calculation prints its progress and final check table, then returns the validated expression when the supported construction succeeds. The two A.+ entries select positive photon helicity in the analytic all-incoming convention. For more control and visible intermediate expressions, continue with the [staged tutorial](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/ConstructingAndCheckingAnAmplitude).

examples.description: Construct a four-point QED amplitude.

name: ConstructingAndCheckingAnAmplitude
title: Constructing and Checking an Amplitude in Stages
summary: Inspect diagrams, preparation, simultaneous completion and the final validation report.

sections.title: Choose the Process and Models
paragraphs: This tutorial keeps the diagrams, prepared expressions and completion reports in separate variables so you can inspect where a simplification or correction occurs. The four-point example uses the QED interaction model for both diagrams and factorization. At higher multiplicity, the factorization model must also contain the complete known lower-point amplitudes.

The particle list fixes the external labels throughout the calculation. Here e and E denote the electron and positron entries in the model, and the two A.+ entries specify the photon helicities. All analytic momenta are incoming.

examples.description: Use one model for both jobs in this four-point example.

sections.title: Generate Diagrams and Channels
paragraphs: [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams) determines which tree diagrams the model allows. [CreateArrowDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateArrowDiagrams) lets you inspect them, while [DiagramAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/DiagramAmplitudes) returns their algebraic expressions together with the mass rules belonging to each diagram.

Generate the factorization targets independently with [FactorizationAmplitudeChannels](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FactorizationAmplitudeChannels). These targets use complete lower-point amplitudes, not the partly simplified diagram numerators that you are trying to repair. Keep this original channel list for the final checks.

examples.description: Generate the diagrams, display them and calculate their amplitudes.
Generate compact physical factorization channels.

sections.title: Prepare Without Throwing Away Information
paragraphs: [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) chooses the requested reference-spinor form and simplifies each diagram with its own permitted assumptions. Its ordinary output is the prepared list. Requesting details here additionally keeps the raw expressions, retained remainders and the preparation history for the next stage.

The `"PreparedAmplitudes"` entry is the part you would inspect to judge whether the diagram expressions have become useful starting points. Passing the entire preparation report to completion also preserves information that would be absent from that displayed list alone.

examples.description: Retain the preparation report.

sections.title: Complete the Physical Residues
paragraphs: [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization) compares the proposed expression with every supplied physical channel and tries to fit the required corrections simultaneously. This avoids repairing one residue while unknowingly spoiling another.

Request details when working through a difficult process. Inspect the report status before continuing: a retained candidate is not a successful amplitude merely because the function returned a report. A timeout or insufficient correction space is information to investigate, not a reason to drop a channel from the comparison.

examples.description: Solve the factorization constraints and retain the compatible family.

sections.title: Complete High-Energy Behavior and Simplify
paragraphs: [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy) receives the retained factorization report, including any remaining allowed correction freedom. It checks the high-energy constraints together with the other obligations rather than assuming every remaining coefficient is fixed by residues alone.

After a successful high-energy stage, retain only the external mass rules with the final expression. [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) can then simplify this complete amplitude using ordinary and external on-shell identities. No diagram-local internal-shell conditions belong to this final preparation.

examples.description: Complete the high-energy stage and extract the final pair.

sections.title: Read the Checks
paragraphs: [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) produces the compact combined report. Start with that table. If a row is unexpected, ask for residues or details to see the actual comparisons rather than guessing from the length of the printed expression.

The explicit seed in these diagnostic examples makes them repeatable. Leave it out for a fresh numerical check. PASS describes the tested kinematics and supported diagnostic; it does not establish a generic symbolic identity or make an unresolved row disappear.

examples.description: Check the final result.
Inspect the actual sampled residues.

sections.title: The Same Workflow in One Call
paragraphs: Once the intermediate stages are familiar, use [ConstructAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ConstructAmplitude) for the same supported workflow in one call. The defaults choose the normal resource settings, so you do not need to copy a long list of tuning options into every calculation.

When you also have an independent Feynman model for the same theory, pass it through `"FeynmanModel"`. The wrapper can then check a fixed factorization or high-energy candidate without first proving that every free family direction is zero. It still requires every standard check and independent Feynman agreement at the normal validation parameter assignments. This is validation of the selected expression, not a uniqueness proof, and the retained family remains in the detailed report. The explicit [CompleteHighEnergy](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteHighEnergy) stage above remains strict when called on its own.

examples.description: Run with normal automatic defaults.

name: ApplyingSpinorIdentities
title: Applying Spinor Identities in a Derivation
summary: Use ordinary reductions and inspect individual legal rewrites.

sections.title: Ordinary Reduction
paragraphs: Start with [ReduceSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReduceSpinorProducts) for ordinary bracket and chain identities. It applies external on-shell relations but does not know a diagram's internal on-shell assumptions. The equal-endpoint massless square bracket below is a simple example whose result you can check immediately.

examples.description: Reduce a self-bracket.

sections.title: Keep Denominators Protected
paragraphs: Use [ApplyToNumerator](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ApplyToNumerator) when a replacement is valid in numerators but must not change denominators. It walks over the additive terms in the expression as supplied. It neither calls Together to combine the fractions nor expands a factored numerator.

This separation matters for constructive internal-shell identities. A numerator relation must not turn the physical propagator denominator of the diagram into zero. [PlainText](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PlainText) is useful when you want to read or save an intermediate spinor expression as text.

examples.description: Replace a numerator symbol while keeping an ordinary denominator untouched.
Inspect the transformed expression in text form.

sections.title: Explore a Single Identity
paragraphs: For a derivation that you can replay, [SpinorIdentityCandidates](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorIdentityCandidates) lists the legal local edits of a `{massRules, expression}` pair. An edit records the identity and the expression pieces it changes. [ApplySpinorIdentity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ApplySpinorIdentity) checks that the edit is still legal before applying it.

The example deliberately disables internal-shell and momentum-conservation moves, so only ordinary identities are being explored. Applying the first listed edit illustrates the mechanism; it does not assert that the first edit is the best simplification. Compare resulting expressions with [SpinorExpressionComplexity](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/SpinorExpressionComplexity), and retain the edit if you want a reproducible route.

examples.description: List ordinary exact edits for a product of angle brackets.
Apply one of the listed identities and inspect the resulting expression.
Compare the expression complexity before and after that edit.

sections.title: Use Known Masses Only Where Valid
paragraphs: When an expression comes from one constructive diagram, its accompanying mass list can justify additional numerator identities. [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) keeps that scope local to the item it is preparing.

Once diagrams have been combined into a complete amplitude, keep only external mass rules for further ordinary simplification. Reapplying every diagram's internal on-shell conditions to the sum would impose incompatible assumptions on different terms. Use the [kinematics tutorial](paclet:HEPCAT/tutorial/KinematicsAndOnShellConditions) to follow that distinction in the full workflow.

name: KinematicsAndOnShellConditions
title: Kinematics, References and On-Shell Conditions
summary: Keep external kinematics, channel residues and diagram numerator assumptions distinct.

sections.title: All External Momenta Are Incoming
paragraphs: HEPCAT writes analytic amplitudes with every external momentum incoming. Consequently momentum conservation is the sum of those incoming momenta equal to zero. The particle order supplies the labels: relabeling the external list changes what 1, 2 and the other integers mean.

Use [ReverseMomentum](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReverseMomentum) when you explicitly cross a symbolic external momentum. The transformation also includes its spinor convention. [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess) performs the crossing automatically from the physical incoming-to-outgoing process, so give that exporter the original all-incoming formula.

sections.title: External and Internal Conditions
paragraphs: External mass-shell conditions describe the external particles of the complete amplitude. These are valid during ordinary spinor reduction. Internal-shell conditions have a narrower role: in the constructive diagram workflow they identify a numerator representative for a particular diagram, or the residue on a specified factorization cut.

The physical propagator denominators stay off shell. [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) uses only the internal conditions actually supplied with an individual constructive item. A completed expression has external mass rules only, and a Feynman diagram has no constructive internal-shell assumptions.

Simplifying a factorization channel on its own cut may change its continuation away from that pole. Keep the original channels as the residue targets. This is why [CompleteFactorization](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CompleteFactorization) can use prepared expressions as useful sources while retaining the original obligations for validation.

sections.title: Reference Choices
paragraphs: Reference spinors describe the massless external polarization choice. The `"PolePreference"` option of [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) controls how those choices are made and also guides the later completion search. AllPhysical favors references with physical denominator structure; AllSpurious favors suitable massless-particle references; Mixed allows both kinds.

A compact individual diagram can be a useful starting point even when its reference denominators introduce apparent spurious poles. Those poles must cancel in the complete correct amplitude. [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes) discovers supported denominator poles and reports whether the sampled comparisons establish the required finiteness.

Feynman diagrams require a consistent reference choice for each massless external leg across the diagram sum. A constructive numerator preparation may make different local choices. In either case, inspect the complete result and its checks rather than judging correctness from the appearance of one diagram.

name: FeynmanComparison
title: Comparing a Constructive Result with Feynman Diagrams
summary: Read a Feynman model, convert its diagrams and compare the same process.

sections.title: Choose Consistent Models
paragraphs: A useful independent comparison needs the same particle properties, masses, couplings and conventions on both sides. Here the constructive QED model supplies the target formula and factorization channels, while the bundled CalcHEP QED model supplies the Feynman rules.

Read each with [ReadModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/ReadModel), keeping them in separate variables. The diagram entry points recognize [FeynmanModel](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanModel) and generate the corresponding tensor expressions.

examples.description: Read both models and select a four-point process.

sections.title: Generate and Convert the Feynman Expression
paragraphs: Generate the Feynman diagrams with [CreateDiagrams](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CreateDiagrams) and convert their complete list using [DiagramAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/DiagramAmplitudes). The intermediate expressions contain Dirac and Lorentz tensors rather than the final bracket formula.

[FeynmanToSpinorProducts](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/FeynmanToSpinorProducts) converts supported tensors using the HEPCAT sign and spin conventions. It applies no internal on-shell conditions, so this result remains independent of constructive diagram-local numerator choices.

examples.description: Produce spinor-product Feynman amplitudes.

sections.title: Prepare with Shared References
paragraphs: [PrepareAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/PrepareAmplitudes) can process the converted Feynman expressions. Its reference selection is shared consistently across the diagrams. The example uses AllPhysical to resolve the explicit Xi spinors into a form suitable for a direct comparison.
Choosing references is not a license to put an internal Feynman line on shell. The preparation recognizes the Feynman input type and retains its off-shell internal algebra.

examples.description: Use a physical-pole preference consistently across the list.

sections.title: Compare with a Constructive Result
paragraphs: Construct the proposed analytic result and the original factorization channels, then pass the independent Feynman expression to [CheckAmplitudes](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/CheckAmplitudes). The report now includes the Feynman comparison alongside the usual consistency checks.

For a disagreement, inspect the detailed report and confirm particle order, crossing, parameters and spin conventions before changing a formula. A sign difference is reported as useful diagnostic information; the checker does not silently adjust the supplied amplitude to force agreement.

examples.description: Construct the corresponding analytic result.
examples.input:
finalAmplitude = ConstructAmplitude[process, qedModel, qedModel];
channels = FactorizationAmplitudeChannels[process, qedModel];

examples.description: Include the independent Feynman expression in the combined report.

name: ExportingToSPINAS
title: Exporting a Numerical SPINAS Process
summary: Export a checked amplitude family, build its numerical code, and compare or integrate it with independent external tools.

sections.title: Collect Analytic Helicity Amplitudes
paragraphs: This tutorial starts with known, checked QED amplitudes and turns them into one numerical process. It separates source generation, compilation, independent validation and event generation so you can choose the stage you need.

The input entries remain in HEPCAT's all-incoming convention. The physical process passed to [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess) determines which momenta are crossed in the generated numerical code. The exporter needs the formulas for the requested helicity combinations, not just a spin-summed squared amplitude.

[LookupAmplitude](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/LookupAmplitude) retrieves the stored four-point formulas from the bundled factorization model. Here the three analytic sectors, together with the exporter's allowed identical-particle permutations, provide the photon-helicity coverage for the unpolarized physical process.

examples.description: Collect the independent photon-helicity cases.

sections.title: Specify Physical Incoming and Outgoing Particles
paragraphs: The rule `{"e", "E"} -> {"A", "A"}` describes electron-positron annihilation to two photons. Generic A requests the photon helicities required by that physical process. A fixed-helicity choice must be explicit if you want only a selected contribution.

The ordinary export writes source files and a README; it does not require a compiler. The returned directory contains the generated process class and build instructions. Keep that directory distinct from the symbolic model files.

examples.description: Write files into a new temporary directory.

sections.title: Build and Run
paragraphs: Set `"Build" -> True` when SPINAS and a compatible compiler toolchain are available. `"RunExamples" -> True` also evaluates the supplied physical example momenta. Building or obtaining a finite example value is useful for checking the numerical interface, but is not an independent validation of the physics.

The generated class has an amplitude function for explicit spins/helicities and a squared-amplitude function with the declared spin average and identical-particle factor. It sums squared moduli of the selected amplitudes; it does not square a sum of their moduli.

examples.description: Build and run the generated example where SPINAS is installed.
examples.input: WriteSPINASProcess[exportDirectory, {"e", "E"} -> {"A", "A"}, entries, knownModel, "ProcessName" -> "eeAA", "Overwrite" -> True, "Build" -> True, "RunExamples" -> True]

sections.title: CalcHEP Validation and Integration
paragraphs: Optional CalcHEP validation generates an independent symbolic reference process and compares squared amplitudes on shared random kinematics. Select CalcHEPDirectory and CalcHEPModel explicitly; neither is guessed. CalcHEPAllowedParticles -> All uses the full selected model, while a visible PDG list selects a smaller reference sector.

The optional n_calchep backend has a different purpose: it connects CalcHEP's numerical integration machinery to the HEPCAT SPINAS matrix element without CalcHEP symbolically regenerating that matrix element. Generated parameter and mass interfaces keep the runtime values consistent.

After building, enter build/results from the exported project directory and run ./n_calchep. If you are already in build, use cd results. This folder contains the actual executable copy, numerical settings and output. It is created inside the CMake build directory, including an alternative build directory selected during configuration, so generated run data stays separate from source. Validation and example programs stay in build. Move the complete results directory elsewhere before deleting build if you want to keep that numerical session. Keep the installed CalcHEP and system runtime dependencies available.

sections.title: Validate Each Photon Helicity with MadGraph
paragraphs: ValidateMadGraph provides an independent numerical check using MadGraph's own generated matrix element. It fixes each massless helicity combination, sums massive-particle spins and evaluates both implementations on exactly the same physical momenta. Masses, couplings, initial-state averages and identical-particle factors must agree.

Select the MadGraph installation, UFO model and particle content explicitly. The example uses sm-full for a massive electron and then MadGraphAllowedParticles -> {11,22} to choose only the electron/positron/photon sector. Without that filter the full Standard Model also contains weak exchange in four-fermion processes. Parameter overrides and maps must match the chosen reference theory; no fitted ratio hides a mismatch.

examples.description: Validate the already exported process.
Keep a replayable diagnostic report.

sections.title: Use the SPINAS Amplitude in MadEvent
paragraphs: The same [WriteSPINASProcess](paclet:HEPCAT/ref/WriteSPINASProcess) export supports two separate MadGraph workflows. ValidateMadGraph compares with an independently generated MadGraph amplitude. The MadEvent numerical bridge instead uses the supplied HEPCAT/SPINAS amplitude for integration and event generation, while retaining MadEvent's phase-space channels, beam settings and cuts.

Select the installation, UFO model and any particle restriction explicitly as in the validation example. Keep the analytic entries in the all-incoming convention; the exporter crosses the declared outgoing legs once. Parameter and mass changes must remain consistent with the supplied amplitude and the chosen numerical model.

This bridge is for supported colorless leading-order tree amplitudes. It does not create the additional matrix elements needed for a next-to-leading-order or matched calculation. Massive-spin correlations cannot be inferred from a spin-summed result or from treating the two libraries' spin bases as identical.

Request "Build" -> True in the same export call. For ProcessName -> "eeAA", enter build and run ./eeAA_madevent --prepare. Compiling the launcher alone does not create the native MadEvent directory; this preparation command does. The default workspace is the compiled project's build directory, determined from its build metadata, so the result is build/PROC_eeAA even if you instead run ./build/eeAA_madevent --prepare from the exported source directory. The PROC_ name follows ProcessName for other processes. The launcher prints the full card, HTML and event-output locations. The first generation step can take longer than later runs because MadEvent builds its integration code.

From the same build directory, ./eeAA_madevent opens the numerical interface and ./eeAA_madevent --run run_01 generates events. Under that working directory, PROC_eeAA/Cards/run_card.dat controls beam energies, cuts, event counts, integration settings and the random seed; PROC_eeAA/Cards/param_card.dat controls numerical model inputs. Open PROC_eeAA/index.html for progress and results, and find the event file in PROC_eeAA/Events/run_01.

Use --work-directory DIR to select another output workspace, or --command-file path to run a normal MadEvent command file. Existing sessions are retained where they were created; use their own bin/madevent program to continue a prepared process. Repeated launches in the same workspace preserve its cards and events.

After --prepare finishes, you can move or copy the whole PROC_eeAA directory to the location where you want to keep the numerical process. Move it outside build before deleting build if you want to keep it. Enter that directory and run ./bin/madevent. Its amplitude sources, headers, HEPCAT/SPINAS numerical libraries and private model support are included, so the original exported project, build directory and SPINAS checkout can be removed without breaking the prepared process. Keep the external MadGraph installation, Python, Fortran toolchain and system libraries available. The outer eeAA_madevent program is the initial setup launcher; the complete prepared directory is the unit to move. Move it between runs while no integration or compilation is active.

The independent comparison remains available through ValidateMadGraph[exportDirectory] and the generated eeAA_validate_madgraph program. The two workflows share the export and selected model while performing different calculations.

examples.description: Export the numerical MadEvent bridge and the independent validator together. Set the installation and model explicitly; this example selects only electrons, positrons and photons.
examples.input:
madGraphDirectory = FileNameJoin[{ParentDirectory[hepcatDirectory], "MadGraph"}];
WriteSPINASProcess[exportDirectory, {"e", "E"} -> {"A", "A"}, entries, knownModel, "ProcessName" -> "eeAA", "Overwrite" -> True, "Build" -> True, "MadGraphDirectory" -> madGraphDirectory, "MadGraphModel" -> "sm-full", "MadGraphAllowedParticles" -> {11, 22}]

sections.title: Run Both Independent References
paragraphs: The two reference checks answer separate questions and both should be available even when one fails. Ask the exporter to run both checks, with an explicit installation and model for each program. The supplied HEPCAT expression is not replaced by either reference result.

A failed requested comparison returns Failure. Its ExportResult retains the generated project and both reference reports, so a CalcHEP failure does not hide the MadGraph result. Compilation or writing source does not by itself establish amplitude agreement. Differences in the selected theory, masses, couplings or conventions must be investigated rather than fitted away.

examples.description: Run both comparisons on the same exported QED helicity family. Replace the installation paths with your selected locations.
examples.input:
calcHEPDirectory = "/path/to/CalcHEP";
exportReport = WriteSPINASProcess[exportDirectory, {"e", "E"} -> {"A", "A"}, entries, knownModel,
  "ProcessName" -> "eeAA", "Overwrite" -> True,
  "CalcHEPDirectory" -> calcHEPDirectory,
  "CalcHEPModel" -> {feynmanModelDirectory, 2},
  "CalcHEPAllowedParticles" -> {11, 22},
  "MadGraphDirectory" -> madGraphDirectory, "MadGraphModel" -> "sm-full",
  "MadGraphAllowedParticles" -> {11, 22},
  "RunCalcHEPValidation" -> True, "RunMadGraphValidation" -> True,
  "ReturnDetails" -> True];

examples.description: Inspect a failed combined comparison without losing the other reference report.
examples.input:
referenceReports = Replace[exportReport, Failure["SPINASValidation", data_Association] :> data["ExportResult"]];
If[AssociationQ[referenceReports], KeyTake[referenceReports, {"CalcHEPValidation", "MadGraphValidation"}], referenceReports]
